div.div: Why the clever guard was turned off: an onset grace of 2 s [I2] cannot tell a 1.5 s greeting [I1] followed by a 200 ms human reply [P3] from the robot hearing itself, so the visitor's first word was rejected and one rejection ended the visit
A. THE NEW OPENING, to scale (one visit, time from the robot's speech onset). Positions of the visitor's reply follow the public turn gap.
processed microphone channel (what the model hears)
ONSET GRACE 2 s [I2]: VAD onsets here are rejected
holds an unanswered greeting, stops listening -> the robot goes idle: the visit is over
greeting ends at 1.5 s; the reply follows after the typical human gap of 200 ms [P3] ->

The guard's design argued 'a rejection costs at most one utterance'. Here that utterance was the first reply to the greeting, so it cost the whole visit. The interaction design changed underneath the defence; the code, tests and promotion rule stayed, only the default moved to OFF (with a boot-log line confirming the setting). A platform audio update had also removed most of the self-hearing it was built for.

(a) THE ROBOT'S OWN MOTORS: impulsive rumble, mostly 60-250 Hz [I12]. Head moving vs holding: raw microphone +8 dB [I8], processed channel +20 dB [I9] (gain control winds up with no speech present); the motion was 3 dB [I10] louder than a nearby talker. Noise-only clips came back as words 5 of 5 times [I11]. Feedback cancellation cannot help: motors have no reference signal.

(b) THE ROBOT'S OWN VOICE: 15 dB [I6] above the room floor during every robot speech window; suppression is late and incomplete, likely because a clipped return is nonlinear and no linear canceller removes it.
C. THE GUARD (what it does when it is on)

Only when VAD would interrupt the robot: for each 200 ms sub-window [I13] at a 50 ms stride [I14], score = 10 log10(E[400-3000 Hz [I15]] / E[rumble band]); keep the MAXIMUM, because one clear vowel is enough. Fail OPEN on any error: 'a deaf robot is a product failure'.
Perfect separation on one robot, one room and one talker is a FIT, not a generalisation.
D. SHIP A GUARD BY A WRITTEN RULE

Shadow mode first (log would-be decisions, change nothing). Default ON needs ALL of: 60 in-scope evaluations [I19]; 15 scripted real barge-ins, none rejected [I20]; 85 % of motor onsets rejected [I21]; a 3 dB worst-case margin [I22].

Every turn-taking change gets TWO measurements, on the robot, moving and speaking, in venue noise: phantom turns caused (false barge-ins, ghost wakes) and real turns lost (rejected barge-ins, missed starts), with sample sizes. Barge-in itself stops the robot only after a 0.4 s debounce [I7].

Legend: purple = robot speech | red = self-hearing, rejection and failure | amber dashed = the onset grace and the guard threshold | green = the visitor's real speech | grey = suppressed channel. Durations and dB are illustrative except the public turn gap.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B4-turn-taking-and-self-hearing.md (how a barge-in is handled, two sources of phantom barge-ins, the spectral barge-in guard, why the clever guard was turned off, 'how it is designed and tested'); Stivers et al. 2009 for the turn gap. [calc]: reply onset = greeting 1.5 s + gap 0.2 s = 1.7 s, which is under the 2 s grace. The reply's length on the canvas is a drawing choice.
[I1] proactive_greeting_illustrative = 1.5 s. illustrative length of a perception-triggered greeting; shorter than guard_onset_grace_illustrative
[I2] guard_onset_grace_illustrative = 2 s. illustrative 'self-hearing grace' after robot speech onset
[P3] turn_gap_typical = 200 ms. public: Stivers et al., 'Universals and cultural variation in turn-taking in conversation', PNAS 106(26), 2009: offsets between turns cluster around a short gap of about 200 ms across 10 languages
[I4] self_hearing_leak_window_illustrative = [0.2, 0.8] s after robot sound onset. illustrative window before late self-sound suppression engages
[I5] self_hearing_suppressed_drop_illustrative = 20 dB. illustrative drop of the processed channel once suppression engages
[I6] self_hearing_lift_illustrative = 15 dB above the room floor on the processed channel during robot speech. illustrative
[I7] barge_in_debounce_illustrative = 0.4 s. illustrative debounce between a 'speech started' event and abandoning the robot's turn
[I8] actuator_lift_raw_illustrative = 8 dB (raw microphone, head moving vs holding). illustrative
[I9] actuator_lift_processed_illustrative = 20 dB (processed channel, head moving vs holding). illustrative; larger than actuator_lift_raw_illustrative because automatic gain control winds up
[I10] motion_over_speech_processed_illustrative = 3 dB (robot's own motion louder than a nearby talker on the processed channel). illustrative
[I11] noise_only_transcripts_illustrative = [5, 5] [attempts producing words, attempts]. illustrative: every noise-only clip sent to a transcription model came back as words
[I12] guard_low_band_illustrative = [60, 250] Hz. illustrative actuator-rumble band
[I13] guard_subwindow_illustrative = 200 ms. illustrative sub-window of the spectral barge-in guard
[I14] guard_stride_illustrative = 50 ms. illustrative stride
[I15] guard_speech_band_illustrative = [400, 3000] Hz. illustrative speech band
[I16] guard_phantom_max_illustrative = 3 dB. illustrative highest score of motor-noise onsets in a fitted set
[I17] guard_threshold_illustrative = 5 dB. illustrative decision threshold on the max sub-window speech-to-rumble ratio
[I18] guard_real_min_illustrative = 8 dB. illustrative lowest score of real speech onsets in a fitted set
[I19] guard_promo_evaluations_illustrative = 60 in-scope evaluations. illustrative promotion criterion
[I20] guard_promo_real_bargeins_illustrative = 15 scripted real barge-ins, none rejected. illustrative promotion criterion
[I21] guard_promo_reject_rate_illustrative = 0.85 fraction of motor-noise onsets rejected. illustrative promotion criterion
[I22] guard_promo_margin_illustrative = 3 dB worst-case class margin. illustrative promotion criterion
